solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scientist off filling rubbish receptacle

indicators.note: the word off goes into the middle of the receptacle, filling it

parts.note: a bin is a container for rubbish

explanation.surface: A researcher is fed up with filling the dustbin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like an adjective about the scientist's mood, but it is taken as written and placed inside BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert, often a backroom researcher.

clue.text: The third to leave party? That's annoying!

indicators.note: the letter standing third in the party word is told to leave, so it is dropped

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone complains when the third guest walks out of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The third' means the third letter of the word for party itself, not a third guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bah is an interjection of irritation or contempt, an exclamation of annoyance.

clue.text: Gift left in market

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word for market

parts.note: a fair can be a market or trade show

explanation.surface: A present has been left behind at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in the sense of a natural talent or aptitude is a flair.

clue.text: Heroin's moved close to coast

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Drugs are being smuggled in near the shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore describes waters or activity near the shore, as opposed to offshore.

clue.text: Shared amount buyable: odd bits have been excluded

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of the phrase leaves only the even-positioned ones

explanation.surface: Something about a shared quantity one can buy, with odd pieces removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual means held in common or reciprocal between two or more parties.

clue.text: Tip from university writer, dismissed at first

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of dismissed

explanation.surface: A tip-off from a university author who was sacked early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads like advice, but it is the verb meaning to overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to upend it, turning it upside down.

clue.text: A French maiden poses — and is revealing

parts.note: un is the French for a
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to pose a question is to ask it

explanation.surface: A French girl strikes poses and shows a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scorecards M stands for a maiden, an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who unmasks a villain is exposing or disclosing them; 'she unmasks' swaps for 'she is revealing'.

clue.text: Notice that contains strangely only two Es, say

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange new way

parts.note: two copies of the letter E

explanation.surface: A remark about a word containing, oddly, just a pair of letter Es.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example', but it is taken as written as part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay eyes on something is to see or spot it, an idiom for noticing.

clue.text: Principal's mood something close to grave?

parts.note: a head is a school principal, with the possessive S
tone can mean the mood or atmosphere of something

explanation.surface: A school head's temper is close to grave, very serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as solemn, matching the head's mood, but it is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone stands next to a burial place, marking it.

clue.text: Gemstone being worn by Yankee with Times

parts.note: clothes being worn are on
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A jewel worn by an American alongside The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: One month in a thousand, indeed!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
ay is an old or dialect form of aye, yes indeed

explanation.surface: An exclamation that one month is rare, one in a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the fifth calendar month of the year.

clue.text: Endanger old New York accord

parts.note: to endanger something is to harm it

explanation.surface: Threatening an old New York agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony and accord both mean agreement or peaceful concord between people.

clue.text: Item of clothing that's disguised hard faces

indicators.note: the letters are disguised by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A garment worn by tough-looking people to hide their features.
explanation.definitionFit: A headscarf is a square of fabric worn over the hair, a piece of apparel.

clue.text: Chaotic study in need of a clean

indicators.note: a chaotic arrangement suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A messy study room needs tidying.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty describes something covered in dust, so it wants cleaning.

clue.text: Old king who's 50 per cent cockney 100 per cent Marxist?

parts.note: 50 per cent is half, which a cockney says as 'alf, dropping the H
a thoroughgoing communist is a red

explanation.surface: Which old monarch was half Londoner and wholly communist?
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century Anglo-Saxon monarch of Wessex.

clue.text: As careless riverside walker did maybe; one Italian director

parts.words: As careless riverside walker did maybe
parts.note: a careless walker by a river might have fallen in, that is fell in
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something a clumsy riverbank stroller did, plus a film-maker from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian filmmaker behind La Dolce Vita and 8½.

clue.text: Long, thick locks securing small minister's houses

indicators.note: the outer word holds the small letter inside it, securing it

parts.note: manes are long thick heads of hair

explanation.surface: Clerics with long hair are securing small homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a Presbyterian or Nonconformist minister.

clue.text: Awful crybaby's ma loves hugs

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it, as if hugging it

explanation.surface: A whining child's mother loves hugs, which is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means extremely bad, terrible in quality.

clue.text: Jenny, perhaps, in novel, reader finally recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are read in reverse order
the letter is placed inside the word for novel

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of reader

explanation.surface: Jenny is a character in a novel the reader finally remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the adjective meaning new; a jenny wren is the traditional name for a female wren.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenny is the name given to a female bird, especially the wren, so the bird is an example.

clue.text: Chap starts on Stitch in Lilo and Stitch

indicators.note: the first letters of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A man begins working on the alien in the Disney film Lilo and Stitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas is a man's given name, so it stands for a chap.

clue.text: US lawman embraced by star in African country

indicators.note: the lawman's letters are held inside the star's

parts.note: the Sun is our nearest star
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American lawyer is welcomed by a celebrity in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in northeast Africa, south of Egypt.

clue.text: Cooker needing beam of light to get very hot

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
to burn is to be extremely hot

explanation.surface: A stove needs a sunbeam to heat up.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rayburn is a British brand of range cooker, a solid-fuel or oil kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayburn is a make of range stove for kitchens, so it is an example of a stove.

clue.text: Only the first sixteen letters in one's head?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the alphabet's opening run, ending at its sixteenth letter
second meaning: colloquial for in the brain, as in having plenty of brains

explanation.walkthrough: P is the sixteenth letter, so the first sixteen letters run from A UP TO P; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Up top is colloquial for the brain or intelligence, as in 'not much up top'.

clue.text: Girl denied son's become boxer

indicators.note: the girl is denied the word, so it is removed

parts.note: Alison is a girl's name
son taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl refused her son a chance to become a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the world heavyweight champion pugilist.

clue.text: Out to lunch midday, ten loudly sent up

indicators.note: out to lunch means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is away for a meal at noon, mocked noisily at ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reads as mocked but means blown upward by explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamited means blown apart with explosives, sending debris skyward with a bang.

clue.text: Doctor yesterday's beginning to be teetotal

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of yesterday

explanation.surface: A doctor began, yesterday, to abstain from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person abstains from alcohol entirely.

clue.text: Mate who's close by day

indicators.note: the word for close sits beside the day abbreviation

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
close as a noun means the end

explanation.surface: A partner who lives nearby during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like the adjective meaning near but is the noun meaning end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a pal or companion, a synonym.

clue.text: Careless agent, cut off internally

indicators.note: the letters for cut off are placed inside the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: A negligent secret agent has been cut off from contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy describes slapdash, untidy work done without proper attention.
